Child Pregnancies In SA

By: Mosibudi Ratlebjane | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We go into the lives Teen Pregnancy,

Unique Selling Point:
The Releasing of the annual Birth Rate release have indicated that a total 1 003 307 birth were registered in South Africa 2020. Of those registered birth a total of 33 899 birth occurred to mothers aged 17 year and younger. Over 688 children aged 10-13 year ( including late birth registrations) gave birth, of these 499 gave birth in 2020.
The number of Teenage Mothers.


Summary:
This has given rise to the questions, if whether or not these numbers are translating to Statutory rape cases and arrests. In this feature we look into the lives of pre-teen and teenage pregnant girls, and the circumstances in which led to the pregnancy. By focusing on two young girls forced into motherhood. At tender ages of between 11: and 16 We look into the reality of their lives, and exposes the true vulnerabilities of young girls in South Africa:

The Sexual Offences Act: Defines, (statutory rape) as: Acts of consensual sexual penetration with certain children (statutory rape).
SAPS National Policy Guidelines for Victims of Sexual offences Girls under the age of 12 years cannot legally consent to sexual intercourse, therefore it will always be rape, irrespective of circumstances. (Under Common law too) Girls between the ages of 12-15 years can be the victims of statutory Rape.

Early pregnancy and motherhood creates a greater risk in terms of maternal complications resulting in low survival rates of babies and forces many girls to prematurely take on adult role which they are not emotionally or physically prepared for.


Further information:
Arrests: Statutory Rape: How many arrests:
Effects of Lockdown; The discrepancies with the DATA: How the number between SAPS, Home affairs do not correlate: The Births and Deaths Registration Amendment Act (Act No. 18 of 2010), stipulates that all births must be registered within 30 days from date of occurrence.


Registration of Fathers:
Information about fathers remain the biggest challenge. In 2020, no reliable information on fathers could be provided due to a high proportion of births registered (more than 60%) without details of fathers. Section 10 of the births and deaths acts prohibits unmarried fathers to have their information on the birth certificate of a child which contributes to the high number of births with no information on fathers. This is expected to change in the coming years as in September 2021 the Constitutional Court ruled that this section of the Registration of Births and Deaths Act is unconstitutional. This means unmarried fathers can now have their information registered in the birth certificate of their children at the Department of Home Affairs.

15 year old, Chantel is in grade 10, is writing her exams carry a heavy load. Everyday her mother Lizzy accompanies her daughter to school, in the mornings for her safety and just in case her daughter gives birth. Chantel, says she was a bubbly and talkative girl, has been very fallen quiet this year and humbled by her pregnancy. She was involved with a 23 year old man and have been dating for some time, when she fell pregnant this year. Lizzy speak about the how the father of the baby is arrogant, stating that she threatened to open a case of Statutory rape, in which he responded he doesn't care. Chantel on the other hand, says that her boyfriend loves her and that her boyfriend has assured her that he will take care of the child. She says they love each other, Her mother has expressed her disappointment, and resents that the father of the unborn child has created a wedge between her daughter while he threatens her future.

COSMO City:
Last year, a 16 year old was raped by a man who lives in the community was excessively being teased at school. The man still roams around free in the community, where the her family has decided to take full responsibility of the child. The baby is two months and is being taken care of by her family.

metadata.Summary: This has given rise to the questions, if whether or not these numbers are translating to Statutory rape cases and arrests. In this feature we look into the lives of pre-teen and teenage pregnant girls, and the circumstances in which led to the pregnancy. By focusing on two young girls forced into motherhood. At tender ages of between 11: and 16 We look into the reality of their lives, and exposes the true vulnerabilities of young girls in South Africa: The Sexual Offences Act: Defines, (statutory rape) as: Acts of consensual sexual penetration with certain children (statutory rape). SAPS National Policy Guidelines for Victims of Sexual offences Girls under the age of 12 years cannot legally consent to sexual intercourse, therefore it will always be rape, irrespective of circumstances. (Under Common law too) Girls between the ages of 12-15 years can be the victims of statutory Rape. Early pregnancy and motherhood creates a greater risk in terms of maternal complications resulting in low survival rates of babies and forces many girls to prematurely take on adult role which they are not emotionally or physically prepared for.
metadata.Further information: Arrests: Statutory Rape: How many arrests: Effects of Lockdown; The discrepancies with the DATA: How the number between SAPS, Home affairs do not correlate: The Births and Deaths Registration Amendment Act (Act No. 18 of 2010), stipulates that all births must be registered within 30 days from date of occurrence. Registration of Fathers: Information about fathers remain the biggest challenge. In 2020, no reliable information on fathers could be provided due to a high proportion of births registered (more than 60%) without details of fathers. Section 10 of the births and deaths acts prohibits unmarried fathers to have their information on the birth certificate of a child which contributes to the high number of births with no information on fathers. This is expected to change in the coming years as in September 2021 the Constitutional Court ruled that this section of the Registration of Births and Deaths Act is unconstitutional. This means unmarried fathers can now have their information registered in the birth certificate of their children at the Department of Home Affairs. 15 year old, Chantel is in grade 10, is writing her exams carry a heavy load.
